heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 1. Run `python --version`, record OS/CPU/thread settings, Python/scikit-learn/pandas/numpy/scipy versions and relevant BLAS info. Compare environment lock files with the original Linux runs and test Python 3.11/3.12-compatible controlled environments if feasible on the machine without damaging other installations.

heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 2. Verify the **raw workbook hash and exactly reconstructed row/identity/outcome counts** against frozen manifests before any model refit. Preserve copies of original legacy result tables under immutable comparison paths.

heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 3. Execute the built-in strict comparator and capture all file-level/field-level differences, including the 14/30 legacy-table mismatch finding. Partition differences into (a) source/cohort or linkage, (b) feature values/leakage, (c) fold or training-order changes, (d) stochastic seeds/threading, (e) dependency/solver/dtype changes, (f) calibration and time-selection changes, (g) formatting and intentionally variable run-time fields.

heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 4. Trace differences using controlled small deterministic fixtures and selected real-data row **fingerprints**, feature and split hashes; keep raw row outputs/private identifiers out of Git. Check as-of transition boundaries, stable group sorting, scikit-learn estimators' solver/preprocessing versions, missing/nullable dtypes, one-hot category ordering, probabilities, clipping, ties in top-capacity ranking and bootstrap seed/RNG choices.

heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 5. Add regression tests specifically reproducing each genuine defect discovered. Repair code only when the science warrants it; write a changelog linking old/new results. **Never widen an arbitrary numerical tolerance to disguise a scientifically consequential difference**. Some numerical disagreement may remain legitimate and must be stated with separate environment-dependent results.

heading: 4. Gate B — reproduce, trace and repair the Windows/Linux numerical discrepancies
requirement: 6. Run a stable environment twice in succession; compare deterministic outputs using a declared substantive tolerance justified by model semantics, plus exact table/schema count checks. Distinguish *within-environment reproducibility* from *cross-platform numeric identity*. If substantive results change, regenerate all affected tables, text, figures and dashboard notices from the same locked run.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 1. Audit exactly how core bundle identity is constructed (corridor, normalised provider, payment instrument, access point, pickup method, pickup location, basket) and how strict identity adds speed and receiving-network coverage. Confirm variable units and survey-collection periods. Preserve original/source values and round-trip canonicalisation tests.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 2. Examine potential **false links, under-links after renaming, collisions, duplicated offerings, relabelled payment instruments, changing network coverage, abrupt 2021/2022 composition changes and 2025 missing wave**. Stratify by origin quarter, region, provider type, speed-change indicators and survey expansion. Do not treat unknown services as confirmed provider exits.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 3. Implement **a reproducible private manual review protocol** for a seeded, pre-specified stratified sample (match vs non-match, ambiguous keys, label drift). Show the user what source fields and cases need human judgement and create a blinded review form/decision guide. The investigator's or another qualified human's adjudications must be recorded **before** calling false-link/true-link rates externally validated. Agent-only inspection is *not* external identity ground truth.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 4. If no external truth source or human adjudication exists, use explicit rule-based **identification intervals** and plausible-linkage scenarios. Report sensitivity of the primary claims without implying a statistically identified mislinkage rate. Do not use provider reputation or commercial availability as ground truth.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 5. Confirm that every numerator/denominator aligns to its estimand. Recompute E1 conditional observed continuity, E2 all-origin bounds, E3 corridor-level survey monitoring, and any E4 variant. Check the 3% and 5% thresholds and USD200/USD500 basket distinctions. Run 2022-era schema/subpopulation shift sensitivities.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 6. Review the 8,914 unknown successors, their subtypes and plausible missingness mechanisms. Show primary nonparametric worst/best bounds first; then separately explain any MAR/IPW assumptions, pattern-mixture/MNAR scenarios and tipping points. IPW and MNAR sensitivity analyses **do not identify truth** without assumptions.

heading: 5. Gate C — service identity, coverage and selection validity
requirement: 7. Connect the measurement finding to a real substantive policy question: **what would a World Bank/SDG monitoring analyst conclude under conditional matched-service continuity versus source-population bounds?** Quantify difference clearly; avoid consumer savings, causal benefit or observed provider exit.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 1. Audit current official RPW dataset catalog and resource list, legal reuse terms and observed collection dates; compare source bytes/hash against 2025Q3 freeze. Search for **genuinely new** 2025Q4, 2026Q1/Q2/Q3 or later official individual-row survey vintages, without assuming they exist. Verify each resource's true observation period, survey fields and official provenance. The previous phase reported that an “updated” web page still yielded the **identical 2025Q3 workbook**.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 2. Revisit archived official report links / Wayback captures only for **evidence the archive actually proves**. The previous effort indexed 125 archived report URLs, but reports/capture timestamps did not identify when every predictor quote became public. Treat archive capture as an *upper bound on first available by*, not precise publication date; distinguish survey collection, report issue label, publication announcement, PDF creation, online capture and file modification.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 3. Assemble an `available_by` registry at **feature/vintage** level. An operational test must satisfy `available_by(feature) <= decision_date < target_collection_start`, for all predictor values used. Never treat an inferred one-quarter history lag as enough if the current-wave quote features themselves had not yet been published.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 4. If a legitimately untouched future wave is found, freeze the existing candidate family and measurement/linkage rules **before reading its outcome**. Seal dataset identity/hashes/timing protocol and only then compute outcomes. Do not retune on the new holdout. Predefine Brier, calibration, baseline comparisons, capacity and group dependence. If the future-wave time information is not provable, call the run **later-period retrospective confirmation** rather than prospective early-warning validation.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 5. If no genuinely new outcome wave is available, retain `NO UNTOUCHED TEST SET`. For a retrospective **measurement-first** paper, determine explicitly whether independent later-wave validation is scientifically essential to the *measurement claim*, rather than inserting a forecasting-only gate that makes any manuscript impossible.

heading: 6. Gate D — historical availability, timing and genuinely new data
requirement: 6. Do not manufacture missing 2025Q2, stitch a 2025Q1→2025Q3 “next quarter” transition, use a new upload date as a new observation or inflate effective sample size by treating correlated quotes as independent seasons.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 1. Evaluate **the one inferential claim that matters** for the selected paper. For Track A, quantify stability of conditional continuity and widening of observed-population bounds under plausible identity and missingness definitions. Use appropriate clustering/dependence; report wave-level summaries and show that results aren't driven by a few very large providers or highly correlated corridors.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 2. Re-evaluate the joint corridor/provider/quarter dependence sensitivity for the *existing* calibrated/model-policy comparisons. Use analytically defensible conservative approaches and sensitivity designs; report the observed small number of independent time waves. The previous attempt's nominal-95% procedure showed **0.86 simulation coverage**. Do not label unvalidated intervals “95% robust” without a verified design/coverage argument.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 3. Keep both **probability quality** and **decision value**: Brier/log loss/calibration, AUROC and failure AUPRC, cost/history/ridge/spline/GBM/RF references, per-year estimates, reliable support counts and both fixed-per-quarter vs pooled monitoring capacity. Pooled rankings that rely on future reobserved membership cannot be portrayed as deployable real-world triage.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 4. At the all-origin level, treat unknown outcomes as unknown. Report identified recall bounds and plausible assumption scenarios; never convert those into observed savings, verified avoided harm or true capacity effectiveness. The earlier 20%-capacity selected-policy all-origin recall bounds were roughly **0.2167–0.5726** and did not identify a unique deployment policy.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 5. If a genuine time-held-out wave exists, perform exactly one sealed confirmation under the predeclared candidate, baseline and comparisons. No reuse of it for tuning/novelty-driven model search.

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 6. Explicitly separate `MODEL COMPARISON RETROSPECTIVE`, `MEASUREMENT CLAIM`, `SOURCE/TRUTH VALIDITY`, and `OPERATIONAL PREDICTION`. If a simple rule is more reliable under fair robust testing, state it prominently; never retain ML as the flagship merely because the project is branded “AI.”

heading: 7. Gate E — valid inference, modelling and practical significance
requirement: 7. Clarify materially whether the measurement difference offers **new actionable interpretation** that prior corridor-level costs obscure. If it does not, say so. A significant Brier improvement cannot rescue a scientifically trivial estimand.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Research title and 4–6 keywords; structured abstract (study purpose, dataset, time frame, estimand, approach, key numerical findings, honest significance, implications).

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Introduction: practical remittance affordability problem; sharp positioning against closest exact-data and comparable-question work; stated materially new contribution.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Methods: data origin/licence; true dates; source-vintage limitations; unit/identity/eligibility; transition/attrition; registered estimands; statistical models; timing split; missingness assumptions; clustering/inference; controls against leakage; ethical/data use; sensitivity scope.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Results: complete record flow; quote-continuity primary estimate and bounds; time/subgroup heterogeneity where credible; strict/core link difference; main statistical uncertainty; carefully interpreted comparative predictive evidence, if justified; figures/tables with accurate denominators.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Discussion: novel scientific lesson, practical interpretation, comparison with closest prior papers, specific limitations (timing, nonreobservation, identity and selection), honest generalizability, future research.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Declarations: **explicit placeholders requiring investigator confirmation** for affiliations, author contributions, funding, conflicts and institutional requirements. Do not invent approvals.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: Accurate bibliography with DOI/URL/publisher, access depth and in-text correspondence. No invented references, unsourced sentences or false exclusion/first claims.

heading: 9. Gate G — write the actual paper if science supports it
requirement: **Supplementary methods** sufficient for replication from lawfully obtained raw data; full sensitivity/robustness tables and figures; transparent research software/data availability statement and AI-assistance disclosure.

heading: 11. Execution order, gates and non-stall rules
requirement: Run one heavy Python job at a time; normally cap `OMP_NUM_THREADS`, `OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS`, `MKL_NUM_THREADS`, `NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS` at **2**; cap tree model parallelism accordingly. Do not spawn repeated workers or fill the drive with duplicate caches.

heading: 11. Execution order, gates and non-stall rules
requirement: Observe available RAM/disk and actual job peak memory. Use chunked/dtype-aware data processing, Parquet caching, restarts and checkpoints where supported. Stop/repair operations causing destructive memory pressure; avoid OS freezes. Keep the laptop awake during long Codex/local execution; a closed/sleeping laptop cannot keep training.

heading: 11. Execution order, gates and non-stall rules
requirement: Prefer the existing Python 3.12 locked analysis environment and do not unpin/change it casually just to make tests pass; CI currently uses Python 3.11 for dashboard/runtime, which is a different purpose.

heading: 11. Execution order, gates and non-stall rules
requirement: Use portable Windows paths and explicit quoting of the space-containing local path; never assume `F:` is mounted in a remote runner.

heading: 11. Execution order, gates and non-stall rules
requirement: Report actual elapsed time and peak RSS if measurable; do not invent resource metrics. No tight arbitrary timebox overrides scientific validity, but checkpoint often enough to survive session interruptions.
